clue.text: Extras: unusual gifts must have been finer?

indicators.note: something unusual is out of its normal shape, so the letters that follow are put into a strange new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone receiving out-of-the-ordinary presents wonders whether they were once better than now.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of both 'gifts' and 'been finer' are rearranged together; the question mark admits the surface is a little strained.
explanation.definitionFit: Perks such as a company car or health insurance are things given on top of salary, which is what extras means.

clue.text: Give quill to person embracing divine protection

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in the arms, so the word for a person wraps around the word for divine

blocks.note: a quill is a large feather, once used as a pen
a being is a living person or creature
DD is Doctor of Divinity, so a divine is a clergyman with that degree

explanation.surface: A request to hand a pen to someone under God's protection, perhaps a scribe in a monastery.
explanation.walkthrough: A divine is a theologian or clergyman, and crosswords often turn it into DD, the degree of Doctor of Divinity.
explanation.definitionFit: Featherbedding is the practice of shielding workers or industries from hardship with excessive jobs, subsidies or cosseting, a kind of protection.

clue.text: Is taking out writ as a result of publication!

blocks.note: taken as written
taking out a writ against someone means bringing a lawsuit

explanation.surface: Someone launches a libel action because of something that was printed about them.
explanation.definitionFit: The issuing of a book or magazine is the act of releasing it to the public, which is what publication means.

clue.text: Professional combatant making a dog trail

indicators.note: making suggests building something new out of the material that follows, so those letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fighter earns a living by laying a scent for hounds to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Roman arena fighters were trained men who fought for a living before crowds, so they were combatants by profession.

clue.text: Square for head of daughter halving fruit

indicators.note: halving splits the fruit into two parts, and the daughter sits in the gap between them

blocks.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter
a common yellow fruit

explanation.surface: A girl cuts a piece of fruit in two, and somehow a headscarf comes into it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandana is a large square of coloured cloth, folded and tied round the head or neck as a scarf.

clue.text: Be drowsy when holding up a favourite jotter

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the words are read from bottom to top, backwards
holding means keeping something inside, so the drowsy word goes round the rest

blocks.note: to nod is to doze off, head dropping
taken as written
a teacher's pet is a favourite

explanation.surface: Someone dozing while propping up their best-loved notebook.
explanation.definitionFit: A jotter is a small book of blank paper for scribbling notes, the same thing as a pad for notes.

clue.text: Nearly forget the blacksmith's shop

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all of it, so the final letter of the word is dropped

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone almost lets the village smithy slip their mind.
explanation.definitionFit: A forge is the workshop with a furnace where a smith heats and hammers metal into shape.

clue.text: Elation dispelled by chiropodist's target

indicators.note: something dispelled is scattered and driven apart, so the letters are broken up and regrouped

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A foot doctor's visit brings someone's good mood crashing down.
explanation.definitionFit: Chiropodists treat feet, and an ingrown or thickened nail on a digit of the foot is one of their usual jobs.

clue.text: Manager's office keeps indefinite number in bed before vessel goes under wave

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so the bed word goes around the number

blocks.note: a cot is a small bed
in algebra n stands for any number
a roller is a long breaking wave
a seagoing vessel

explanation.surface: A boss's room oddly contains a numbered bed, while a boat sinks under the swell.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry the ship going under the wave means it is placed after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Controllership is the post or position of a controller, someone who manages finances or operations, so it is a manager's office in the sense of role.

clue.text: Don't vote for sailor with moral taint

blocks.note: AB is an able seaman
a stain on one's character is a moral blemish

explanation.surface: Advice not to back a seaman with a dubious reputation at the polls.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstain is to decline to cast a ballot either way when a motion is put.

clue.text: Poor Ted rebuilt underwater missile

indicators.note: something rebuilt is put together again in a new form, so these letters are reassembled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Unlucky Ted has had to reconstruct a weapon for use beneath the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A torpedo is a self-propelled explosive weapon launched from a submarine or ship to travel below the surface.

clue.text: One in hat meets another one where Port-au-Prince is

indicators.note: in places the first word inside the headgear word

blocks.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one
a second Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A man wearing a hat encounters someone else in the Caribbean capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Port-au-Prince is the capital city of the Caribbean nation sharing Hispaniola with the Dominican Republic.

clue.text: Don't upset this street vendor's barrow

definitions.text: Don't upset this street vendor's barrow

blocks.note: surface reading: a warning not to tip over a trader's stall
setter's reading: the idiom about not upsetting it means not spoiling a plan, and the barrow is the fruit-seller's one in that saying

explanation.surface: A warning to passers-by not to knock over a market trader's handcart.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'upset the apple-cart' means ruin a carefully arranged plan, and the cart itself is a costermonger's barrow of fruit.

clue.text: Indispensable assistant makes correct offer

definitions.note: the answer is the adjective, as in right-hand man; the definition stands for the whole phrase

blocks.note: right means correct
to hand something is to offer or pass it

explanation.surface: A trusted aide puts in the proper bid.
explanation.definitionFit: A right-hand man or woman is the most trusted helper, the one a leader could not do without.

clue.text: Oil of turning leaf

indicators.note: turning suggests something churning over, so the preceding letters are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Oil pressed from a leaf that is changing colour in autumn.
explanation.definitionFit: A folio is a single sheet of a book or manuscript, numbered on one side only, which is also called a leaf.

clue.text: I'm not charged for jest about dance at church

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the jest word goes round the dance word

blocks.note: jest and fun are both light-hearted joking
a reel is a lively Scottish or Irish folk dance
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Someone protests they are not being accused of a joke about a dance in church.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition speaks as the answer: a meal that nobody has to pay for.
explanation.definitionFit: A free lunch is a meal or benefit that costs the recipient nothing, so it could say it is not charged for.

clue.text: He composed part of "Squirrel Garden"

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a stretch of letters lying inside the quoted title

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A composer wrote a section of a piece called Squirrel Garden.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make it look like a real work title, but it is just a string to search.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Elgar was the English composer of the Enigma Variations and the Pomp and Circumstance marches.

clue.text: Useless information: front of bus seen in garage

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept
seen in places one thing inside another, here within the building

blocks.note: taken as written
its opening letter

explanation.surface: Pointless trivia: the nose of a bus visible inside a vehicle depot.
explanation.definitionFit: Garbage literally means rubbish, and figuratively nonsense or worthless data, as in the computing phrase garbage in, garbage out.

clue.text: British government's spotless foyer

blocks.note: something spotless is pure white
a hall is an entrance lobby

explanation.surface: The UK government has an immaculately clean entrance lobby.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay rather than showing possession.
explanation.definitionFit: Whitehall is the London street lined with ministries, so its name stands for the British civil service and government.

clue.text: Set down a bird, keeping it on time

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the bird word goes around the rest

blocks.note: a wren is a tiny brown songbird
used unchanged, as it appears in the clue
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Instructions to land a bird and make it stay punctual.
explanation.definitionFit: Set down here means recorded on paper, so a thing set down has been put in writing.

clue.text: In improper regions you'll get cold shoulders

indicators.note: something improper is not in its correct form, so the letters must be put into a different order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Behave badly in certain areas and people will snub you.
explanation.definitionFit: To cold-shoulder someone is to deliberately pay them no attention, which is to snub or disregard them.

clue.text: A no-good pin-up of an ancient race

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the pin word is written from bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
NG is the usual abbreviation for no good
a nail is a metal pin

explanation.surface: A worthless poster picture from some prehistoric tribe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pin-up' reads as a single word for a glamour photo but splits into pin plus a direction.
explanation.definitionFit: The Angles were a Germanic people who settled eastern England, and Anglian describes things belonging to that early tribe.

clue.text: About extending speech for the East, for example

indicators.note: extending means stretching, so the speech word is stretched open to take the other inside

blocks.note: diction is manner of speaking
re means concerning, about

explanation.surface: A note on lengthening one's talk to suit an Oriental audience.
explanation.definitionFit: East is one of the compass points, so it is an instance of a way to face or travel.

clue.text: Inch is equal to another with a hundred up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means everything before it is written from bottom to top

blocks.note: a peer is someone's equal
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A measuring statement: an inch matches another unit, with a hundred added on top.
explanation.definitionFit: To inch is to move forward very slowly, a little at a time, which is how one creeps.

clue.text: Mix up gruel with this pistol

indicators.note: mixing up stirs things into a different arrangement, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Stirring porridge with a handgun, an absurd kitchen scene.
explanation.definitionFit: The Luger is a semi-automatic handgun designed in Germany and widely used by its army in both world wars.

clue.text: Most tidy swallow in the nest

indicators.note: in places the swallowing word inside the home of the bird

blocks.note: taken as written
to swallow food is to eat it

explanation.surface: The neatest swallow sitting in its nest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallow' looks like the bird, fitting the nest, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat means orderly and trim, so the superlative form is the most orderly of all.

clue.text: His turn to become undersized?

indicators.note: to become is to change into something else, so the letters are turned into a new word

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: It is now this person's go to be the small one.
explanation.definitionFit: The runt is the smallest and weakest animal in a litter, so runtish describes something stunted and small.

clue.text: Remain cheerful as when shaving

blocks.note: first meaning: the idiom for staying brave and optimistic
second meaning: literally, tilting the head back so the razor reaches the throat

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense takes the idiom literally: when shaving the neck, you hold your jaw raised.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to stay hopeful in difficulty, and literally describes lifting the face to shave beneath it.
